Relative Elemental Amounts under a Two-Stage LTE Model

Source: R/saha-boltzmann.R
ls_saha_boltzmann.Rd

Estimates a common Boltzmann temperature and relative elemental number fractions using explicit atomic and instrumental inputs. The Saha equation accounts for the neutral/singly-ionized balance. This research calculation requires optically thin emission, local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), a common sampled plasma, stoichiometric ablation and corrected spectral response. It does not establish those assumptions from an observed spectrum.

Usage

ls_saha_boltzmann(
  x,
  elements,
  lines_nm,
  electron_density = NULL,
  window_nm = 0.5,
  verbose = TRUE,
  atomic_data = NULL,
  partition_functions = NULL,
  ionization_energies_ev = NULL,
  temperature_k = NULL,
  intensity_scale = c("energy", "photon"),
  wavelength_medium = NULL,
  tolerance_nm = 0.01
)

Arguments

x

A ls_spectrum() with resolved, baseline-corrected lines.

elements

Unique character vector of elements to include.

lines_nm

Named list of measured line wavelengths per element.

electron_density

Independently estimated electron density in cm^-3. Required; no density is assumed.

window_nm

Integration width in nm. Default 0.5. Effective integration windows, including the coarse-channel expansion of ls_peak_area(), must be disjoint, wholly inside the measured wavelength range and contain at least three measured channels each.

verbose

Logical. Report the temperature and scope of the result.

atomic_data

A data.frame with one unambiguous record per selected transition: element, ionization (1 = neutral, 2 = singly ionized), wavelength_nm, wavelength_medium ("air" or "vacuum"), wavelength_vacuum_nm, A_s (transition rate in s^-1), g_upper (statistical weight), energy_upper_ev (relative to that ion's ground state), response (measured signal per relative emitted intensity), and source (the transition reference). These data must be supplied explicitly; the bundled historical line compilation is insufficient for this calculation. For vacuum records the two wavelength columns must agree within 1e-8 + 1e-8 * wavelength_nm nm (numerical rounding only).

partition_functions

Named list, one entry per element. Each entry is a list with neutral and ionized, each either a function of temperature in kelvin returning the partition function, or an explicitly chosen positive constant approximation. Use the same statistical-weight convention as g_upper and include the relevant energy levels.

ionization_energies_ev

Named positive numeric vector of first ionization energies in eV, one per element.

temperature_k

Optional independently estimated common temperature in kelvin. If NULL, estimate it from a shared slope with a separate intercept per element/ion stage. Estimation requires a full-rank fit and positive residual degrees of freedom. Non-negative slopes are rejected.

intensity_scale

"energy" (default) or "photon", describing the response-corrected integrated intensities. Energy intensities require the vacuum-wavelength factor; photon counts do not.

wavelength_medium

Medium of the measured axis. If NULL, read x$metadata$wavelength_medium; an unspecified medium is an error.

tolerance_nm

Maximum difference between requested and reference wavelengths. Default 0.01. Multiple possible transitions are an error.

Value

A tibble with element, temperature_k, concentration_rel, electron_density, n_lines, r_squared and log_population_sd. Fractions are normalized only over the supplied elements, under a model that excludes molecules and charge states above +1; they are neither mass fractions nor absolute sample concentrations. log_population_sd measures line/stage disagreement on the log population scale, not calibrated uncertainty. Attributes line_diagnostics, assumptions, and temperature_source retain the calculation's inputs and limitations.

Details

Earlier versions silently used unit statistical weights, omitted partition functions and ignored electron density. Those outputs cannot be reused as quantitative reference results. Supply verified physical inputs and refit. A low residual does not verify LTE, optical thinness, absence of self-absorption, spectral resolution, detector response or matrix-independent ablation.

References

NIST Atomic Spectra Database, spectral lines and Saha/LTE documentation: https://physics.nist.gov/PhysRefData/ASD/Html/lineshelp.html.
